overview: Constellation Energy is the largest generator of carbon-free electricity in the United States, operating the country's biggest nuclear fleet alongside wind, solar, hydro, and (following the January 2026 Calpine acquisition) a major natural gas, geothermal, battery storage, and retail-supply platform. Spun off from Exelon in 2022 and headquartered in Baltimore, the combined company now controls roughly 55 GW of generating capacity (~22 GW nuclear) across five reportable segments (Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, New York, ERCOT, Other Power Regions) plus Calpine's competitive retail electricity business. It sells power and energy products to utilities, municipalities, cooperatives, and commercial/industrial/public-sector/residential customers, and is increasingly positioned as the primary supplier of firm, carbon-free power to hyperscale data centers.

business_model.summary: Constellation earns revenue from wholesale and retail electricity sales generated by its nuclear, gas, and renewable fleet, supplemented by long-term bilateral power purchase agreements (PPAs) with utilities and, increasingly, data-center operators, plus capacity market payments from PJM and other RTOs. The Calpine acquisition (closed Jan 7, 2026, ~$26.6B total consideration including ~$12.7B assumed debt) added a large natural-gas/geothermal fleet and a competitive retail supply business serving ~62 TWh/year of load, roughly doubling the balance sheet (shareholders' equity ~$14.9B to ~$33.8B; total debt ~$7.5B to ~$17.4B per Q1 2026 metrics).

revenue_streams.name: Long-term data-center PPAs (Microsoft/Crane, CyrusOne, and other hyperscalers)
Renewables (wind, solar, hydro) and other power regions

business_model.customer_type: B2B/wholesale (utilities, municipalities, cooperatives) and large commercial/industrial customers including hyperscale data-center operators, plus retail commercial and residential supply via Calpine's retail platform
business_model.geographic_mix: Concentrated in PJM footprint (Mid-Atlantic, Midwest/Illinois), with New York, ERCOT (Texas), and Other Power Regions segments; Calpine adds meaningful ERCOT and Western/geothermal exposure

competitive_position.market_position: Largest U.S. nuclear operator (~22 GW nuclear, ~55 GW total generation post-Calpine) and the clear scale leader among competitive/merchant power generators bidding for data-center load; positioned as the preferred counterparty for large, credit-worthy hyperscale customers seeking firm carbon-free baseload power

moat_factors.description: Largest US nuclear fleet provides irreplaceable, licensed baseload carbon-free capacity that cannot be easily replicated given multi-decade construction timelines and NRC licensing barriers for new nuclear
NRC operating licenses, PJM interconnection queues, and decades-long construction lead times for new baseload capacity create very high barriers for new entrants

moat_factors.factor: Long-term contracted revenue with premium counterparties
moat_factors.description: 20-year PPAs with Microsoft (Crane/Three Mile Island restart), CyrusOne, and others lock in premium pricing and de-risk merchant exposure
Addition of flexible gas, geothermal, and battery storage plus a retail supply arm broadens the offering to data-center and C&I customers seeking firm dispatchable capacity alongside nuclear baseload
Long operating history and safety record as a nuclear operator supports counterparty trust for multi-decade contracts

weaknesses: High exposure to PJM capacity market design/price-cap decisions, which caps upside even in tight supply years
Integration risk and financial leverage step-up from the large, still-fresh Calpine acquisition
Merchant/wholesale power price exposure for uncontracted generation creates earnings volatility tied to power and gas prices
Regulatory divestiture obligations (DOJ/FERC-mandated asset sales) reduce some acquired capacity and create execution risk/timeline pressure

growth_drivers: Data-center/AI-driven electricity demand growth, with Constellation positioned as a preferred supplier of firm, carbon-free power (Microsoft/Crane Clean Energy Center restart, CyrusOne 380 MW deal, and additional pipeline of >5,650 MW of long-term clean energy agreements)
Nuclear uprates: ~1 GW of planned uprates over the next decade (including 135 MW at Braidwood and Byron) backed by ~$3.9B of planned capital spending
Three Mile Island / Crane Clean Energy Center restart targeted for 2027, adding ~835 MW of carbon-free capacity under a 20-year Microsoft PPA
Calpine acquisition synergies: expanded generation fleet (~23 GW added), retail supply platform (~62 TWh/year load), and cross-selling opportunities across combined footprint
Rising PJM capacity auction clearing prices (2028/29 BRA cleared at the $325/MW-day cap; Constellation cleared 18,875 MW, ~$2.2B of capacity revenue for that delivery year)
Long-term base EPS growth target of 20%+ from 2026 through 2029
Federal policy tailwinds supporting nuclear (U.S. policy goal to quadruple nuclear capacity by 2050)

business.description: Absorbing a ~$26.6B acquisition that roughly doubled the balance sheet creates operational, systems, and cultural integration risk

DOJ/FERC resolution requires divestiture of five PJM generating assets, one ERCOT asset, and Calpine's Gregory Power Plant stake within 240 days of close (by Sept 4, 2026); first sale (Brazos Valley, $860M to LS Power) announced Aug 2026, but full completion and pricing of remaining divestitures carries execution risk
Heavy reliance on PJM capacity and energy markets exposes the company to a single RTO's rules, congestion, and demand dynamics
A meaningful part of the growth thesis rests on continued hyperscaler AI capex and power demand; any slowdown in data-center buildout would reduce the value of the long-term PPA pipeline

financial.description: Total debt roughly doubled from ~$7.5B to ~$17.4B and net debt/EBITDA rose to ~3.0x following the acquisition, reducing balance-sheet flexibility
50 million new shares issued as Calpine merger consideration diluted existing shareholders, though offset by accretive share repurchases per management commentary
Uncontracted generation and the newly added gas fleet expose earnings to natural gas and power price volatility

regulatory.description: FERC-accepted price collar (~$325/MW-day cap, ~$175/MW-day floor) extended through the 2029/2030 delivery year limits upside from capacity auctions even when the market clears at the cap in tight years

regulatory.risk: Nuclear licensing risk for Crane/TMI restart
regulatory.description: Restart requires NRC operating license approval (decision expected ~May 2027) plus state/local permits; any delay or denial would push back or jeopardize the Microsoft PPA economics
Ongoing obligation to complete divestitures on the DOJ-mandated timeline; failure to execute could trigger penalties or further remedies
Potential future FERC/PJM market design reforms (e.g., further price cap changes, capacity accreditation rules) could alter revenue predictability

macro.description: Higher debt load post-Calpine increases sensitivity to interest rate levels and refinancing costs
Calpine's predominantly gas-fired fleet increases exposure to natural gas price swings, affecting margins on uncontracted generation
A pullback in hyperscaler capital spending on data centers would reduce demand growth underpinning the long-term contract pipeline
Power demand is relatively defensive/inelastic versus broader consumer discretionary sectors, providing some insulation, though C&I demand can soften in a downturn

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. power demand is inflecting upward after two decades of flat load growth, driven by data centers/AI, electrification, and reshoring of manufacturing; nuclear is enjoying a policy and market renaissance as the preferred firm, carbon-free baseload source, with federal policy targeting a quadrupling of nuclear capacity by 2050
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - power demand is relatively defensive, but merchant/wholesale price exposure and capacity-market outcomes introduce cyclicality tied to gas prices, weather, and reserve margins
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - higher debt load post-Calpine (net debt/EBITDA ~3.0x) increases sensitivity to rate levels for refinancing and capital-intensive nuclear uprate/restart projects
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Minimal - almost entirely domestic USD revenue and costs
key_input_costs: Capital equipment for uprates and restart projects

recent_developments.event: Closed acquisition of Calpine Corporation for ~$26.6B total consideration (50 million new CEG shares + ~$4.5B cash + ~$12.7B assumed debt), adding ~23 GW of gas/geothermal/battery/solar capacity and a competitive retail supply platform serving ~62 TWh/year
FERC accepted PJM tariff revisions extending the capacity market price collar (~$325/MW-day cap, ~$175/MW-day floor) through the 2029/2030 delivery year
FERC approved a PJM interconnection rules waiver supporting the Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island) restart
NRC released a draft Environmental Assessment finding no significant impact for the Crane/TMI restart; 30-day public comment period held

PJM's 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction cleared the entire RTO at the price cap of $325/MW-day; Constellation cleared 18,875 MW (up from 17,950 MW prior auction), implying ~$2.2B of capacity revenue for that delivery year

Reported Q2 2026 results: GAAP EPS of $1.42 (down from $2.67 y/y due to Calpine purchase accounting/one-offs) but adjusted operating EPS rose to $2.55 from $1.91; raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $11.50-$12.50 from prior $11.00-$12.00

Agreed to sell the Brazos Valley Energy Center (606 MW gas plant in ERCOT) to LS Power for $860 million, the first of the DOJ/FERC-mandated Calpine divestitures (due within 240 days of close, i.e., by ~Sept 4, 2026)
Morgan Stanley raised its price target on CEG from $364 to $369, maintaining Overweight; broader analyst consensus (~19 Buy/3 Hold of 22 analysts) carries an average target near $348

items.notes: Raised from prior $11.00-$12.00 guidance; based on expected average diluted shares outstanding of ~357 million; driven by commercial business outperformance, higher realized customer margins, portfolio optimization, and accretive share repurchases, partially offset by higher O&M from performance-related compensation
Reflects contribution from Calpine integration, nuclear uprates, and new long-term data-center PPAs
Enhanced target following Calpine deal and expanded contracted generation pipeline
Supports ~1 GW of planned nuclear uprates, including 135 MW at Braidwood and Byron
Includes Microsoft (Crane/TMI), CyrusOne (380 MW), and other data-center/utility contracts

guidance.management_commentary: Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance after a strong Q2, citing outperformance in the commercial business, higher realized customer margins, and accretive buybacks. Longer-term, management reiterated 20%+ base EPS growth through 2029 and an enhanced 2029 base EPS target, underpinned by the Calpine integration, nuclear uprate program, and the growing pipeline of long-term data-center power contracts. Management also continues to emphasize progress on the Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island) restart, targeting NRC license approval around May 2027 and return to service later that year.

bull_case: Largest U.S. nuclear fleet gives Constellation an effectively irreplaceable position to supply firm, carbon-free baseload power to hyperscale data centers at a time of accelerating AI-driven electricity demand
Long-term, high-value PPAs (Microsoft/Crane-TMI, CyrusOne, and a growing >5,650 MW pipeline) provide multi-decade, premium-priced, contracted revenue visibility that reduces merchant price risk
Calpine acquisition roughly doubled scale, added flexible gas/geothermal/battery capacity and a retail supply platform, diversifying the generation mix and broadening the addressable customer base
Record PJM capacity auction clearing prices (at the $325/MW-day cap) plus rising cleared MW for Constellation directly boost near-term capacity revenue (~$2.2B for the 2028/29 delivery year)

Management has repeatedly raised guidance (FY2026 adjusted EPS raised to $11.50-$12.50) and reiterated an ambitious 20%+ base EPS CAGR through 2029, with strong analyst support (19 of 22 rate Buy, average target ~$348 vs. recent price near $262)
bear_case: Leverage increased materially post-Calpine (net debt/EBITDA ~3.0x, total debt roughly doubled to ~$17.4B), reducing balance sheet flexibility and increasing sensitivity to rates and refinancing risk
PJM's capacity price collar caps upside even when the market clears at its ceiling, meaning capacity revenue growth is bounded by regulatory design rather than pure market forces

Integration risk from a large, complex acquisition (Calpine) including mandatory, DOJ/FERC-imposed divestitures on a tight timeline, which could distract management or realize below expected sale proceeds

The Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island) restart, a key growth pillar, still depends on NRC license approval expected only around May 2027, leaving execution/regulatory timing risk embedded in the growth story

Valuation already prices in substantial AI/data-center optimism (shares trade well above pre-Calpine, pre-AI-boom levels), so any slowdown in hyperscaler capex or delay in contracted project delivery could compress the premium multiple
